question: Which of the following folk artists became the first dhaki to win a Padma Shri in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gokul Chandra Das**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gokul Chandra Das**, a renowned **dhaki artist**, became the first dhaki to receive the prestigious Padma Shri award in **2025**. This recognition highlights the contribution of traditional folk art to India's cultural heritage.
 
• A **dhaki** is a traditional drummer who plays the **dhol**, especially during the festival of **Durga Puja** in West Bengal and other parts of eastern India. Their rhythmic beats are an integral part of the festive celebrations.
 
• Gokul Chandra Das was honored for his exceptional dedication to preserving and promoting the **art of dhaki drumming**, which has been a part of India's intangible cultural heritage for centuries.
 
• The Padma Shri award, India's **fourth-highest civilian honor**, is given for distinguished contributions in various fields, including art, literature, sports, and social work.
 
• This award has brought attention to folk artists who often remain underrepresented despite their significant contributions to India's cultural fabric.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors in India, instituted in **1954**. They include Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
• The awards are conferred by the President of India and recognize excellence in various fields such as **art, literature, social work, public affairs, science, and sports**.
 
• Padma Shri is awarded for distinguished contributions, and recipients are selected through nominations vetted by committees.
 
 
 
• **Dhaki Tradition:**
 
 
• Dhakis are traditional drummers, primarily found in **West Bengal, Odisha, and Assam**. They play the **dhol**, a large drum, during various celebrations, especially **Durga Puja**.
 
• The beats of dhakis serve as a call to devotees during religious ceremonies and create a festive ambiance.
 
• Dhakis often wear traditional attire and perform synchronized movements while drumming, adding to the visual appeal of their performance.
 
 
 
• **Durga Puja:**
 
 
• Durga Puja is a major Hindu festival celebrated across India, especially in **West Bengal**. It marks the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon Mahishasura.
 
• The festival is characterized by grand decorations, idol worship, cultural performances, and the rhythmic beats of dhakis.
 
• Dhaki drummers play a pivotal role in enhancing the spiritual experience of the festival through their vibrant and energetic beats.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Folk Artists:**
 
 
• Folk artists contribute significantly to preserving India's **intangible cultural heritage**. Their recognition through awards like Padma Shri helps in promoting and safeguarding these traditions.
 
• Such honors bring attention to marginalized communities and encourage younger generations to continue practicing traditional art forms.
 
• Artists like Gokul Chandra Das serve as **ambassadors of cultural heritage**, inspiring others to appreciate and sustain India's rich traditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Leander Paes:** An Indian tennis legend known for his numerous Grand Slam victories and contributions to Indian sports. However, he is not associated with dhaki drumming or Padma Shri for folk art.
 
• **Mary Kom:** A celebrated Indian boxer and Olympic medalist, known for her achievements in sports. She is unrelated to the folk art of dhaki drumming.
 
• **Anant Nag:** A veteran Indian actor known for his work in Kannada cinema, but he has no association with the traditional art of dhaki drumming.
